items.title: David Finck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 29, 2015
items.q: I mean Ray Brown used to really drive hard with Oscar [Peterson] — they would rush but who cares?

ctx.x: Now is that true for drummers too? I’ve had people sort of debate about playing on top of the time, playing behind the time, and then some people say, “the time is the time.” Like if you’re on top of the time then you’re rushing.

Well I don’t know that I agree with that statement. I think that there is a way where music leans forward and leans backward. And we’re not machines. And even with a click track you can lean forward and it can be okay. And I always felt like there was some classic rhythm sections where the bass player might be a little ahead of the drummer, if you really put it up on a screen and analyzed it. And it feels unbelievable. And for whatever reason. I mean Ray Brown used to really drive hard with Oscar [Peterson] —…

you listen to Basie’s band, you know certain figures, they sit back. There’s a great record of Peggy Lee singing Cy Coleman’s “I’ve Got Your Number.” And there are a couple of horn figures where you can just hear — the lead trumpet player must have said, “we’re playing it like this.” And they just play the figure just a little more relaxed than the rest of the band is. And it’s great. I mean to me that’s the music.
